subject.title: Model configuration accepts unvalidated model names, enabling silent misconfiguration

question: Should unknown configured model refs be warning-only in doctor/config validate, hard validation errors, or left to startup/runtime warnings when catalog authority is incomplete?
rationale: The implementation seam is clear, but the behavior affects custom providers, future model names, provider auth/catalog availability, and upgrade safety, so automation should not choose the permanent warning/error contract alone.

options.title: Warning-first validation
options.body: Add catalog-backed doctor/config validate warnings for unknown configured refs, with clear wording for untrusted or custom catalogs and no hard failure by default.

options.title: Strict validation
options.body: Reject unknown configured refs at config validation time, accepting a compatibility break unless an escape contract or migration path is added.

options.title: Runtime-only handling
options.body: Keep config validation permissive and rely on runtime errors, status, and fallback notices instead of adding a new analyzer.

recommendation.title: Warning-first validation
recommendation.body: Add catalog-backed doctor/config validate warnings for unknown configured refs, with clear wording for untrusted or custom catalogs and no hard failure by default.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest observed history across model selection, provider identity, and the current validation/model-ref collector lines.
